question: How many paintings from the Rijksmuseum are in the collection?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:museum "rijksmuseum" }
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings in this graph whose source museum is the Rijksmuseum. The graph only holds paintings made between 1850 and 1900, so this counts that slice of the collection, not the whole museum.

question: How many paintings by Claude Monet are there?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p . ?p rdfs:label "Claude Monet" }
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings, across all three museums, that are plainly attributed to Claude Monet. Works only 'after' or 'attributed to' him are not included.

question: Which Vincent van Gogh paintings does the Met have?
sparql: SELECT ?w ?title WHERE { ?w mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum "met" ; dcterms:title ?title . ?p rdfs:label "Vincent van Gogh" }
explanation: Lists paintings at the Met that are plainly by Vincent van Gogh. Works only attributed to him or made 'after' or by an 'imitator of' him are left out.

question: Which artists have paintings in all three museums?
sparql:
SELECT ?artist (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?paintings) WHERE {
  ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?museum .
  ?p rdfs:label ?artist .
}
GROUP BY ?p ?artist
HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) = 3)
ORDER BY DESC(?paintings)
explanation: This finds artists whose paintings appear at all three museums (Rijksmuseum, Met and Art Institute of Chicago) and shows how many of their paintings the graph holds. It counts only works plainly by the artist, not those merely 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' them.

question: How many artists have works in more than one museum?
explanation: This counts the artists whose paintings are held by at least two of the three museums. It only counts works plainly by the artist, so works merely 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' someone are left out.

question: Show me landscapes at the Rijksmuseum.
explanation: This finds Rijksmuseum paintings whose subject has a label containing "landscape" (such as "landscape" or "landscape painting"). It includes both subjects the museum recorded and subjects suggested by AI.

question: Which Impressionist paintings show snow?
explanation: Finds paintings whose museum-stated style or the artist's Wikidata movement is Impressionism and whose subjects include snow. The subjects include both those the museums recorded and those an AI model suggested from the image.

question: How many paintings have subjects that were suggested by AI rather than recorded by the museum?
explanation: This counts paintings that have at least one AI-suggested subject (confidence 0.6 or higher) that the museum did not also record for that painting. It does not count paintings that simply have no museum-recorded subjects at all.

question: Which paintings did the AI tag with night that the museum didn't?
explanation: This finds paintings the AI linked to the subject "night" (suggestions with confidence of at least 0.6) and keeps only those where the museum's own recorded subjects include no concept labelled "night".

question: When was Berthe Morisot born and when did she die?
sparql: SELECT ?birthYear ?deathYear WHERE { ?p rdfs:label "Berthe Morisot" . OPTIONAL { ?p mc:birthYear ?birthYear } OPTIONAL { ?p mc:deathYear ?deathYear } }
explanation: This looks up the person record labelled exactly "Berthe Morisot" and returns her birth and death years as stored in the graph. The years are optional, so the person still appears even if one of them is missing.

question: Which artists in the collection belong to the Hague School?
explanation: Lists the people whose movement, as recorded on Wikidata, is the concept labelled "Hague School". It does not include artists linked only through the related Impressionism concept.

question: How many paintings were begun in the 1880s?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:beginYear ?y . FILTER(?y >= 1880 && ?y <= 1889) }
explanation: Counts the paintings whose begin year falls between 1880 and 1889, across all three museums.

question: How many paintings does each museum have?
sparql: SELECT ?museum (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:museum ?museum } GROUP BY ?museum ORDER BY DESC(?n)
explanation: Counts the distinct paintings (made 1850–1900) held by each of the three museums in the graph: Rijksmuseum, the Met and the Art Institute of Chicago.

question: Which five artists have the most paintings?
sparql: SELECT ?artist (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p . ?p rdfs:label ?artist } GROUP BY ?p ?artist ORDER BY DESC(?n) LIMIT 5
explanation: Counts the paintings plainly credited to each artist across all three museums and lists the five with the most. Works only 'after', 'attributed to' or 'workshop of' an artist are not counted.

question: Find paintings of boats from before 1870.
explanation: This finds paintings begun before 1870 whose subjects mention boats (including words like "sailboat" or "rowboat"). It includes both subjects the museums recorded and AI-suggested ones.

question: How many artist records were matched by a person approving an AI suggestion?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?a) AS ?records) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?p) AS ?people) WHERE { ?p mc:sourceAgent ?a . ?a mc:matchMethod "human-approved" }
explanation: This counts museum artist records whose match method is "human-approved", meaning a person reviewed and confirmed the match. It also counts how many distinct people those records belong to. The graph doesn't record whether the proposed match came from an AI, so the count covers all human-approved matches.

question: How many paintings are not open access?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work . FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?w dcterms:license ?license } }
explanation: Counts the paintings that have no licence recorded. In this graph, a missing licence means the museum's record is not open access.

question: Which paintings are only attributed to, after, or imitating Vincent van Gogh?
explanation: Lists paintings whose link to Vincent van Gogh is only qualified (for example 'attributed to', 'after', 'imitator of', 'workshop of'). It matches qualified-artist labels containing 'van gogh' and shows the attribution wording.

question: Portraits of women at the Met
explanation: This lists Met paintings that have a portrait subject and a subject about a woman or women. A single subject such as "portrait of a woman" counts for both, and AI-suggested subjects are included alongside the ones the museum recorded.

question: Which Impressionist painters have works in more than one museum?
sparql:
SELECT ?artist (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) AS ?museums) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?museum; separator=", ") AS ?whichMuseums) WHERE {
  ?p mc:movement ?m ; rdfs:label ?artist .
  ?m skos:prefLabel ?ml . FILTER(LCASE(STR(?ml)) = "impressionism")
  ?w mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?museum .
} GROUP BY ?p ?artist
HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?museum) > 1)
ORDER BY DESC(?museums) ?artist
explanation: This finds painters whose Wikidata movement is Impressionism and counts how many of the three museums hold works plainly by them, keeping those with works in at least two. Works only 'attributed to' or 'after' an artist are not counted.
